question: Measles coverage of 95% stops outbreaks on paper. What does one case do in a neighbourhood where fewer people are immune?
answer: It spreads, because the unvaccinated cluster. Measles passes to about 15 people in a group with no immunity, so chains die out only above about 93% immune. New York City's 2018–19 outbreak, about 650 cases, ran almost entirely through a few close-knit Brooklyn neighbourhoods where coverage sat far below the city's average.
move: An average across a whole area hides the pocket where things break.
ask: Where in my life does a reassuring average hide one weak spot that could fail?
source: Zucker et al., NEJM, 2020; Anderson & May
reference: Zucker et al., Consequences of Undervaccination: Measles Outbreak, New York City, 2018-2019, New England Journal of Medicine, 2020; Anderson & May, Infectious Diseases of Humans: Dynamics and Control, Oxford University Press, 1991

notes.text: Half immune: one case seeds nearly 500 more within five weeks.
80% immune: each case infects three, and one becomes about 40.
About 93%: the tipping point. Each case infects roughly one other.
The city's average: chains fizzle out after a case or two.
